assignment.title: Draft grading evaluation: stack vs queue basics
assignment.description: Explain the difference between a stack and a queue. The answer should cover the access order, core operations, and at least one suitable use case or example for each structure.

dimensions.name: correctness
dimensions.criteria: Correctly explain LIFO vs FIFO and the basic operations of both structures.

dimensions.name: completeness
dimensions.criteria: Cover access order, operations, and at least one example or use case for each.

dimensions.name: clarity
dimensions.criteria: Explain the contrast clearly with coherent wording and structure.

assignment.reference_answer: A stack follows LIFO and typically supports push, pop, and top/peek. It is suitable for function-call stacks, undo operations, and expression evaluation. A queue follows FIFO and typically supports enqueue, dequeue, and front/peek. It is suitable for task scheduling, BFS traversal, buffering, and waiting-line style processing.
